title: Synthetic calibration generator and runtime drift guard for FP8 mode selection (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Enable safe, automated FP8 (E4M3 / E5M2) rollout on Hopper by combining a synthetic calibration data generator with a runtime drift-guard that prevents cross-batch activation scale regressions. This ticket builds the calibration dataset pipeline, implements sentinel telemetry for activation variance, and provides a canary + rollback plan for staged rollouts. Goal: unlock FP8 savings without regressions in key quality metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic calibration dataset generator produces representative activation distributions for all production models and returns per-layer histogram summaries
Automated selector achieves stable mode choice (E4M3 vs E5M2) with <1.0% latency variance in steady-state for our canary shards
End-to-end evaluation shows no more than 0.5% average regression on the primary eval suite (perplexity/ROUGE/embedding-cosine as applicable)
Runtime drift guard prevents activating FP8 mode when cross-batch activation-sigma increases by >2.5x relative to rolling baseline
Canary rollout can be completed and, if necessary, rolled back within a single deployment window (<= 30 minutes) using existing rollback tooling
tasks: Design synthetic calibration seedsets and variability knobs (length, prompt styles, tokenization edgecases)
Implement generator service that outputs per-layer activation histograms and synthetic input bundles
Extend calibration pipeline to run synthetic suites at scale and store profiles in model-bundle metadata
Implement runtime drift-guard: sentinel metrics, thresholding, and safe-disable API
Add telemetry dashboards (per-shard and per-layer) and alerting for drift/safety thresholds
Run offline accuracy sweep comparing E4M3/E5M2/INT8/FP16 on core models and surface results
Create canary rollout runbook and automated rollback hook
Write QA tests and a CI job for calibration reproducibility
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Calibration, and Observability teams. Agreed on baseline metrics (activation-sigma, cross-batch variance, output delta).
2025-02-18: MVP synthetic generator implemented; produces per-layer histograms and jittered prompt variants against small model set.
2025-02-24: Calibration runs for 3 core models completed; E4M3 shows lower latency but one model exhibited output drift on long-context tests. Opened investigation (linked PR).
2025-03-01: Runtime drift-guard prototype pushed (PR #12489). Guard exposes soft-thresholds and opt-in force-enable flag for experimentation.
2025-03-04: Canary plan drafted; observability dashboards wired with baseline panels. Preparing canary run next week.
review_feedback: PM review (J. Lin): prefer conservative defaults for public customers; canary first for internal-only pools
Safety review (SRE): require explicit telemetry retention for 90 days for postmortem of any regressions
Design (R. Santos): add synthetic edgecase suite covering tokenization mismatches and composed system prompts
Runtime (K. Mori): suggested moving sentinel evaluation from per-request to per-epoch aggregation to avoid noise-induced disables
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic datasets may not capture rare activation tails -> Mitigation: include production-sampled seeds and adversarial mutation for tail amplification
Risk: Runtime noise causes false positives for drift guard -> Mitigation: use rolling-window aggregation and hysteresis before disabling FP8
Risk: Canary regression impacts tenants -> Mitigation: run canaries on isolated internal pools and enforce throttled traffic percentages
Risk: Telemetry costs grow -> Mitigation: sample at shard-level and store aggregated histograms instead of raw activations
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal calibration - run synthetic generator across all candidate models and store profiles (duration: 3 days)
Phase 1: Internal canary - enable FP8 behind opt-in flag for 5 internal shards, monitor telemetry for 48 hours
Phase 2: Gradual ramp - expand to 20% of traffic on low-risk pools with automatic rollback on threshold breach
Phase 3: Customer opt-in - expose conservative FP8 profile for Dedicated customers with SLA guardrails
Phase 4: Full default - enable for eligible models with monitoring and monthly calibration re-run
notes: Prefer conservative default mapping: prefer E4M3 for activations with high per-layer kurtosis; E5M2 for tensors known to benefit from exponent range
We will keep INT8 fallback for models that fail end-to-end evals; implement coarse-grained per-model mode pinning
Telemetry retention and privacy: all activation histograms are aggregated and anonymized; raw inputs are not stored
Coordinate with Legal before making telemetry available outside core infra team
